title: Vagal Insufficiency Syndrome (VIS): A Unifying Hypothesis for the Pathophysiology of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Long COVID
content: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and Long COVID (LC) are chronic multisystem conditions for which no biomarker, or disease-modifying treatment currently exists. This is largely due to the failure to identify the underlying primary pathology as well as the remarkable heterogeneity of patients and their disease severity levels. We propose that ME/CFS and LC are, in most cases, a common dysautonomic state we term Vagal Insufficiency Syndrome (VIS). VIS describes a chronic deficit in vagal tone arising from damage, or dysfunction, of the brainstem-vagus axis (BVA). We argue that the known functions of the vagus nerves map closely onto the symptom profile of both conditions. Additionally, we reason that heterogeneous symptomatology is the expected outcome of vagal neuropathy because they have an organotopic, fascicular structure. In this paper we present the current evidence that the BVA is abnormal in patients, outline potential mechanisms whereby VIS could cause postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and post-exertional malaise (PEM), and consider potential upstream aetiologies. VIS is offered as a unifying and falsifiable model, with specific research directions and clinical considerations.
